title: Teacher Workflow No. 09: your discussion prompt asked for agreement and got it
author: Doan Winkel
source: How to Teach With AI (howtoteachwithai.substack.com), November 16, 2026
summary: This installment of Doan Winkel's Teacher Workflow series argues that online discussion boards fill with agreeable, interchangeable posts because the prompt itself offers a safe answer, and that a chatbot or a student who skipped the reading can produce those posts equally well. It gives a step-by-step routine using any chat tool: pull the three deadest prompts, have the AI write the safest possible post and name the wording that made agreement easy, then rebuild each prompt around a forced choice between two positions defensible from the reading. A balance check guards against a straw-man side B, and a fake-post test with no attachment checks whether the prompt can be answered without opening the reading. The routine adds reply starters that require naming specifics and a reply instruction asking students to name the evidence that would change their mind. A short tally of counts closes the loop, and a smallest version is offered for teachers short on time.
points: A prompt with one defensible position makes agreement the cheapest post, so the fix is in the prompt, which is the one thing the instructor controls.
Rebuilding a prompt around a forced choice works only if both sides come from the attached reading and each has citable evidence, since a chat tool with no text will invent sides.
Run a fake-post test in a fresh chat with only the prompt text; if the result would earn participation credit without the reading, the prompt can be answered from vibes.
Asking students to name the evidence that would change their mind turns pile-ons into real argument.
Tracking simple counts (sides picked in sentence one, replies quoting a classmate, replies to the opposite side) shows whether the new prompt is working.
quotes: A discussion prompt with a safe answer is a compliance check with a word count.
The prompt has one defensible position and every student can see it. Agreement is the cheapest post on the board.
Find the three boards since September with the most “I agree” replies and the fewest replies that quoted anyone.
The sides have to come from the text, and a chat tool with no text will invent them, locations and all.
If one side is the obvious right answer and the other is a position nobody in your field would hold, the discussion dies again, just with a side B nobody picks.
Name the evidence that would change your mind” ends the pile-on. A student who can’t name it joined a team.
A 90/10 split on the sides means side B is still a straw man. Fix side B before you blame the students.
Don’t rebuild the course. One prompt, steps 2 and 3, one chat, ten minutes.
